title: Shared Redis token bucket lets pods exceed the partner API limit and starves steady traffic
measures: The limiter does get -> compute -> set against a shared store, so concurrent callers in different pods spend the same token (including the first write for a new key and the refill written on denial), and its refill rounds tokens down and resets the timestamp, so traffic faster than one token per gap never refills; drifting pod clocks must not move the timestamp backwards either. The tempting fix (an in-process per-key mutex plus fractional refill with negative elapsed time clamped) passes the single-pod scenario from the issue, but hidden tests run several limiter instances on a store with interleaving latency, a deterministic clock with time moving while calls are in flight, skewed pod clocks and acquire() waiters, and check exact admission counts and the capacity + rate*T budget.
prompt:
Acme 429s again: our rate limiter isn't holding

We got Acme 429s three times this week and a warning that the account gets suspended for an hour next time. Our limiter is set to 45 req/s (capacity 45, ratePerSec 45) and Acme's limit is 50/s, so we should have margin. Their logs show bursts of 70-80 requests in a second from us, always when the month-end autoscaling kicks in (we go from 6 to 12 sync pods, plus the cron jobs, all on the same Redis).

The weird thing is that the opposite happens too. When the shipment sync runs as a steady stream (it's about 60-70 req/s of demand, so it should just get the 45/s), `acquire()` lets the first burst through and then almost everything sits waiting or times out with RateLimitError. Grafana shows us doing ~0 req/s to Acme for minutes at a time while the queue backs up.

Locally I can reproduce something: 20 concurrent `tryTake('acme')` calls in one process with the memory store and a capacity of 5 all come back allowed. docs/rate-limits.md has what the limiter has to guarantee and our deployment facts (pod clocks drift by up to ~1 s). The store interface (memory/Redis) is in the README; please don't add Redis-only tricks, the memory store and Redis store must both work.

commits.message: feat: shared token-bucket limiter for the Acme client
